title: Theodore Roosevelt to John Hay, coded telegram of 27 May 1903 (Library of Congress, Roosevelt Papers reel 413 frame 0026): the State Department Red Cipher of 1876, read by William Echols

documents.shelfmark: Library of Congress, Manuscript Division, Theodore Roosevelt Papers, reel 413, frame 0026 (Theodore Roosevelt Center record o266250)
documents.route: Theodore Roosevelt -> John Hay (Secretary of State)

plaintext.source: The Theodore Roosevelt Center record describes it only as a coded message; no decipherment was found by the contributor or in the repository.

transcription.source: the contributor's transcription of the Library of Congress scan; the project did not see the scan
transcription.notes: A typed telegram; 23 five-digit groups, four spelled letters, several clear words (of, think, it, junketing, at, the), two cancelled groups.

system.summary: The State Department Red Cipher of 1876 (J. H. Haswell): five-digit groups, the first three digits the printed page and the last two the entry, with a spelling table keyed by the first group for names the book lacks.

prior_solution.where: The Roosevelt Center record gives no decoding and the contributor found none; the codebook is an archived key (NARA T1171 roll 1, online; a repository note says it is printed in Weber 1979, not consulted here) not previously connected with this telegram. The same codebook is used in the 1918 Kobe telegrams (targets/kobe1918), a separate correspondence.

conditions.human_role: William Echols submitted the transcription, the key identification and the reading (issue #353), made with GPT-6.1 Sol in Codex. The project checked the submission for internal coherence and, on 14 Nov 2026, checked every codebook entry used on the NARA page images; it has not seen the scan of the telegram.

solution.what: The contributor transcribed the typed telegram from the Library of Congress scan; the project did not see the scan.

The contributor identified the 1876 State Department Red Cipher as the key, using a clue from Florentijn van Kampen's study for the group 10000, and read the 23 groups and the spelled letters (K I E L) from its pages.
Project check: 23 groups (22 distinct) each have an entry in key_excerpt.tsv and the replaced text is a coherent English telegram (VERIFICATION.md). No scan or codebook page compared.

Project check of the key on the codebook itself: NARA T1171 roll 1 (catalog id 417267710), found online in the integration of PR #561 (targets/kobe1918). Each of the 22 distinct groups looked up on its page image (images listed in key_excerpt.tsv) and the spelling code division 1, page 579 (image 0577), with the key 56169: all 22 entries agree with the contributor's, and U A W C read K I E L. The scan of the telegram is still not seen, so the transcription is not checked.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): all 22 distinct codebook groups of the telegram looked up on the NARA page images of microfilm T1171 roll 1 (catalog id 417267710, catalog.archives.gov/medialz, fetched one image every 5 s): every entry in key_excerpt.tsv is the printed 'Message or true reading' of that page and number (e.g. 561 69 What is the, 412 76 Object, 184 27 British government, 473 72 Request, 339 00 I, 528 44 Do not think, 253 61 Desirable, 536 64 Trip, 384 01 Should be made, 531 49 To, 368 85 Judgment). Film image = printed page - 3 up to about p. 370, page - 2 above. The roll's NARA target sheet (image 0004) reads 'Cipher and Key, July 1, 1867'; the book's title page (image 0006) reads 'Cipher and Key.' without a date, so the '1876 Red Cipher' name was not confirmed. Not checked: the spelling table for KIEL (U a w c) and the telegram scan.

validation.notes: A codebook lookup with 22 distinct groups; the coherence of the decoded sentences is the evidence, and no n-gram test applies.

texts.label: Telegram of 27 May 1903, Roosevelt to Hay (LoC Roosevelt Papers reel 413 frame 0026)
texts.summary: Roosevelt, asks the Secretary of State what the object of the British government's request is, says he does not think it desirable that the trip should be made a junketing one, and says that if they touch at an English port it should be after the trip to Kiel, in his judgment.

reading_review.note: Read the decipherment as English sentences: the 23 groups replaced by their entries build a coherent telegram; the transcription is the contributor's and was not compared with the scan; the codebook entries were checked on the NARA images on 14 Nov 2026.
